blocks.text: Imagine you are at a market in Lagos, and you need to find the shortest path to another stall. Vectors can help you determine this displacement efficiently.

blocks.markdown: Vectors are mathematical entities used to represent quantities that have both magnitude and direction. In this lesson, we will focus on 2-dimensional vectors, which are often represented as column vectors.

blocks.title: Column Vector
blocks.text: A column vector is a way of representing a vector in two dimensions, typically written as $\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$, where $x$ and $y$ are the components of the vector along the horizontal and vertical axes, respectively.

blocks.markdown: Vectors can be added together and multiplied by scalars. These operations are useful in various applications, including physics and engineering.

steps.text: Identify the components of each vector.
Combine the results into a new column vector: $\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$.

blocks.markdown: Scalar multiplication involves multiplying each component of a vector by a scalar (a real number). This changes the magnitude of the vector but not its direction.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always double-check your vector operations, especially the signs of the components, to avoid common mistakes in exams.

points: Vectors can be represented as column vectors with two components.
You can add vectors by adding their corresponding components.
Multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its magnitude.
